classification.difficultyReason: Apply the familiar half-scale midpoint triangle and halve the parallelogram area; one short linkage of two supplied midpoint facts.

content.prompt: $X$ and $Y$ are the midpoints of the sides PS and SR of a parallelogram PQRS. Prove that the area of triangle SXY is one eighth the area of the parallelogram.

answer.worked: The two triangles SXY and SPR have the same included angle at S, while $SX=\frac{SP}{2}$ and $SY=\frac{SR}{2}$. They are similar by SAS with scale factor 1/2, so their areas have ratio 1/4. Equivalently, their corresponding bases and perpendicular heights are each halved. The diagonal PR divides parallelogram PQRS into two equal-area triangles, so $[SPR]=\frac{[PQRS]}{2}$. Consequently $[SXY]=\frac{[SPR]}{4}=\frac{[PQRS]}{8}$.
